case.title: The archive case
case.setup: On Monday morning, a small mechanical prototype was missing from its usual place in a local history archive. Nobody has yet verified where it went.
case.instruction: Read the observation, then choose which interpretation you find more persuasive. Your choice changes what you examine next.

a.title: An administrative mix-up
a.description: Your choices mostly favoured ordinary errors, incomplete records and routine activity. The object might have been misfiled or shifted in storage without its records being updated.
a.verify: Check the physical storerooms, reconcile inventory versions, and speak to the staff responsible for the records.
a.caution: Nothing in the displayed clues establishes that a routine mistake actually happened.

b.title: An unrecorded exhibition transfer
b.description: Your choices mostly favoured coordinated preparation. The object might have been temporarily moved for a future exhibition before the paperwork was completed.
b.verify: Look for signed transfer authorisations, transport manifests, exhibition plans and a physical confirmation of the object's location.
b.caution: Nothing in the displayed clues establishes that a planned transfer actually happened.

clues.title: The empty cradle
clues.observation: A catalogued prototype was absent from its usual storeroom shelf on Monday morning. Its digital record still listed that location.
clues.context: The last confirmed sighting was the previous Thursday. There is no verified record of its movements since.

choices.label: The location record may simply be out of date.
choices.meaning: A record-keeping lapse could explain the discrepancy.

choices.label: Its movement may have been arranged but not entered.
choices.meaning: A deliberate move could have preceded the administrative update.

clues.title: A corrected inventory
clues.observation: A handwritten inventory count is lower than the electronic total by exactly one item. The handwritten correction is not initialled.
clues.context: No date was recorded beside the correction.

choices.label: An unverified correction is more likely a counting error.
choices.meaning: The discrepancy may be unrelated to a physical movement.

choices.label: Someone may have counted the object as already moved.
choices.meaning: The handwritten total could reflect a movement not yet in the system.

clues.title: A borrowed key
clues.observation: A spare storeroom key was signed out on Friday and returned on Monday. The log records no purpose for the loan.
clues.context: Staff sometimes borrow this key for general maintenance.

choices.label: The key loan could be an ordinary maintenance visit.
choices.meaning: The access log, by itself, does not identify a reason for entry.

choices.label: The timing could fit an organised relocation.
choices.meaning: The borrowed key may have enabled a planned movement.

clues.title: “Move the special piece”
clues.observation: A loose note reads: “Monday — move the special piece.” The author is unknown, and the item is not identified.
clues.context: The note was found among ordinary storage and event-planning papers.

choices.label: It may refer to routine rearrangement of storage.
choices.meaning: The phrase is too vague to connect confidently to the missing prototype.

choices.label: It may refer to moving a specific object for an event.
choices.meaning: The instruction could describe purposeful preparation.

clues.title: A weekend delivery
clues.observation: A delivery vehicle was admitted to the archive on Sunday. The gate register shows a time, but not the contents of its load.
clues.context: The archive also receives routine deliveries of packing material and supplies.

choices.label: The visit may have been unrelated to the object.
choices.meaning: A vehicle at the site is not evidence of what it carried.

choices.label: The vehicle might have been used to move it.
choices.meaning: The visit creates a possible transport opportunity, not a confirmed transfer.

clues.title: An unfinished event poster
clues.observation: An undated draft poster advertises an upcoming exhibition of historical inventions. It contains no list of objects to be displayed.
clues.context: No final exhibition schedule has been located.

choices.label: The exhibition might have nothing to do with this item.
choices.meaning: An event theme is not a confirmed object list.

choices.label: The prototype could be part of the planned display.
choices.meaning: The draft offers a possible motive for an authorised move.

clues.title: The incomplete paperwork
clues.observation: A blank transfer form was found in the archive office. There is no signed form in the available file, but the file may be incomplete.
clues.context: The archive's procedure normally requires a signed transfer authorisation.

choices.label: The missing authorisation weighs against a planned transfer.
choices.meaning: It may be more plausible that nobody formally arranged the movement.

choices.label: The form may have been prepared but never completed.
choices.meaning: A genuine plan might exist even if its paperwork was unfinished.
